canvas-01.description: The left half of printed sheet 1 of the 1928 Clinton atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the top. It shows Halstead Street running north out of the town centre from its junction with Water Street, up to the town limits at the top of the sheet, with the South Branch of the Raritan River curving along the east side of the lots and crossed by a steel bridge at the bottom right. Water Street runs west from Halstead at the bottom of the sheet, and Clinton Avenue, a 20-foot street, runs north from Water a short way west of Halstead. Development is thin and residential: frame dwellings with sheds, coops and barns on long lots along the east side of Halstead backing onto the river, and a few houses along Water Street and Clinton Avenue. Institutions are the Roman Catholic church on the east side of Halstead in the upper part of the sheet, the M. E. Church and its parsonage near Water Street, and a gymnasium and grand stand standing in open ground west of Halstead. A cemetery is marked at the top right, against the town limits line. Most of the land west of Halstead is left empty, with block numbers only. A four-inch and a six-inch water pipe run along Halstead and Water. The right half of the same page, holding the water and fire department notes, the title cartouche, the key map at 800 feet to an inch, the legend and the street and specials index, lies outside this part. Sheet numbers 2 and 3 in the lower margin refer to the adjoining sheets.
notes: Clinton Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap under that name; a modern unnamed service way leaves Water Street at about the same place and was used as a hand-picked point.

The part is placed from the Halstead Street / Water Street junction, the Clinton Avenue point and one parcel block corner on the east side of Halstead between lots 367 and 368, about 530 m north; low confidence.
Town limits are drawn across the top of the sheet.

Printed sheet 1. Left half: map at 100 ft to an inch, Halstead Street north of Water Street with Clinton Avenue and the South Branch of the Raritan River, north up. Right half: water and fire notes, title cartouche, key map at 800 ft to an inch, legend and street and specials index (masked out). One part.

sheet-2-1.description: Downtown Clinton at 100 feet to an inch, drawn with north towards the upper left. Leigh Street runs across the top of the part from the steel bridge over the South Branch, where Halstead Street and Water Street come in from the west, past Center Street, East Main and Main Streets and Beaver Avenue to High Street. Center Street curves south-west past the Clinton Flour Mill to meet Main Street, the commercial street, which crosses Spruce Run and the South Branch on a steel bridge to Quarry Street, where Thompson Bros. grinding mill stands by the dam. W. Main runs south from Leigh past a filling station, over the concrete and steel bridge and down the middle of the sheet to Hancock Street at the bottom. Main Street is lined with stores, the post office, Smith's garage, banks, a plumber and an electrical shop. South of the river the Clinton House stands at the fork of Quarry and W. Main, and east of W. Main are the L.V.R.R. Clinton Branch depot, freight house and coal pockets, the Fox Bros. coal and lumber yard, a garage and motion picture house in the Music Hall, the ice houses of the Clinton Milk Co. and the Clinton Foundry Co., marked not in operation. The rest is dwellings on long lots. Beaver Brook runs diagonally through the open lots at the upper right. A not-named street and a no-exposure note mark the right edge. The inset at the lower left of the sheet, W. Main further south-west, is a separate part.
notes: W. Main north of the South Branch and Beaver Avenue north of Leigh are today Old Highway 22; south of the bridge W. Main is Old Highway 22 (CR 513) and then West Main Street.
Center south of Leigh is today Lower Center Street.
Main Street / Quarry Road was not detected; the drawn street pattern between the steel bridge and W. Main differs from today's.
Placed from six street junctions, five of them along or near Leigh Street; fitted scale about 3 percent larger than the Annandale sheet.

Downtown Clinton at 100 ft to an inch, turned about 55 degrees (north to the upper left): Leigh and Halstead Streets, Center, Main and East Main, W. Main (Old Highway 22) across the South Branch to Hancock, Quarry, the L.V.R.R. Clinton Branch depots. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset in a heavy box at lower left, W. Main further south-west with the State Highway and a not-named road.

sheet-2-2.description: An inset in a heavy-ruled box at the lower left of sheet 2, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned like the main map, with north towards the upper left. It continues W. Main south-west of the main map, out past the town limits, which cross the inset diagonally. W. Main runs down the right side of the inset with lots numbered in the 300s on both sides. Near the top, the State Highway, 50 feet wide, comes in from the left and meets W. Main; lower down a 40-foot not-named road leaves W. Main to the west, and below it W. Main narrows to 35 feet and bends towards the south-east. The block between the State Highway, W. Main and the not-named road is block 13; block 12 lies above with a row of dwellings and a concrete shop on W. Main, and block 14 below with a farm group of a barn, sheds, an ice house and a dwelling. Most buildings are frame dwellings with outbuildings on deep lots; the land is otherwise open. A north arrow and the sheet's scale bar sit in the open ground of the inset, and a no-exposure note runs along its bottom edge.
notes: The State Highway is today the stretch of West Main Street west of Pittstown Road, and W. Main south-west of the junction is today Pittstown Road, cut by the Interstate 78 / US 22 interchange; the not-named road has no modern counterpart.

Placed on the single junction where the State Highway meets W. Main (today Pittstown Road / West Main Street), with the scale and rotation of the main part of the sheet (anchored, low confidence). The top of the inset then overlaps the bottom of the main map by about 40 m, although the lot numbers suggest it continues beyond it; the position along W. Main may be off by that much.

Downtown Clinton at 100 ft to an inch, turned about 55 degrees (north to the upper left): Leigh and Halstead Streets, Center, Main and East Main, W. Main (Old Highway 22) across the South Branch to Hancock, Quarry, the L.V.R.R. Clinton Branch depots. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset in a heavy box at lower left, W. Main further south-west with the State Highway and a not-named road.

sheet-3-1.description: North-east Clinton at 100 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper left. Center Street runs up the left side of the sheet from Leigh Street, at the bridge over the South Branch, past New Street and two not-named streets towards the north-east. E. Main runs north from Leigh to New, and Beaver Avenue follows Beaver Brook north from the steel bridge on Leigh. Along the bottom, Leigh Street continues east past High and Alton, with Main St. and W. Main St. leaving it to the south. The block between Center, New, E. Main and Leigh is the town's commercial edge: the Union House hotel and a bank at Center and Leigh, the town hall and fire department, the H. Mains silk mill, auto repair shops, a printing and insurance office and the Commercial Shirt Co. factory. Up Center Street are the Presbyterian Church and a cemetery, with dwellings on long lots on both sides. Along Leigh east of Beaver Brook stand the Baptist Church and parsonage, and behind High Street the public school. A second cemetery lies east of Alton. The South Branch of the Raritan River runs along the left edge. Heavy lines cut off the upper right of the sheet and two strips along Leigh Street, which are drawn as separate parts.
notes: High is today School Street; Beaver Avenue is part of Old Highway 22; Alton is Alton Place; the two not-named streets off Center are today Central Avenue and George's Place.
Alton is marked 'arbitrary' for its house numbers.

North-east Clinton at 100 ft to an inch, north to the upper left: Center, New, East Main, Beaver Avenue, Leigh, High and Alton. Four parts separated by heavy lines: part 1 main map (left and bottom); part 2 top right, Center Street further east with Harrison (turned differently); part 3 strip of Leigh Street lots 301-342 east of Alton; part 4 box at lower right, Leigh Street lots 401-410 further south-east.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: strip: Leigh Street lots 301-342, east of the main map (no street junction; position along Leigh Street not identifiable; needs step 6b: match lot lines to parcel corners along Leigh Street).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: box: Leigh Street lots 401-410, further south-east (no street junction; needs step 6b: parcel corners along Leigh Street).

sheet-3-2.description: The upper right of sheet 3, cut off from the main map by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. It shows Center Street further east than the main map, running diagonally up the part, with Harrison Street meeting it from the north at the middle. The town limits run along Harrison and then across the part on a dash-dot line. Dwellings with sheds and garages stand on narrow lots on both sides of Center Street, numbered in the 400s and 500s, with a group of outbuildings near Harrison; the rest is large open blocks numbered 4, 9 and 76. Two dash-dot match lines lettered A and B cross the part towards the main map. A compass rose is drawn in the open ground on the dividing line.
notes: Placed on the single junction of Center Street and Harrison Street with the scale of the main part of the sheet and the rotation of the measured street lines (anchored, low confidence).
Today Center Street runs east here and Harrison Street north from it, as drawn.

North-east Clinton at 100 ft to an inch, north to the upper left: Center, New, East Main, Beaver Avenue, Leigh, High and Alton. Four parts separated by heavy lines: part 1 main map (left and bottom); part 2 top right, Center Street further east with Harrison (turned differently); part 3 strip of Leigh Street lots 301-342 east of Alton; part 4 box at lower right, Leigh Street lots 401-410 further south-east.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: strip: Leigh Street lots 301-342, east of the main map (no street junction; position along Leigh Street not identifiable; needs step 6b: match lot lines to parcel corners along Leigh Street).

sheet-4.description: The New Jersey Reformatory for Women, located a mile and three-quarters west of the Clinton post office, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the top. The grounds are laid out on arbitrary internal roads: B Court runs north and south through the middle with a turning loop at each end, 1st Place crosses it in the upper part and leads east towards Clinton, 2nd Place crosses it lower down and ends in a loop at the west, and A Court runs diagonally from 2nd Place to a loop at the west end of 1st Place. The institution's buildings are drawn in pink as fireproof or tile construction: Paddock Hall with its cells, Whittpen Cottage, Silzer Cottage, a cottage added from plans, Fielder Cottage, the Alexander Chapel with a school in its basement at the head of B Court, the laundry, a storage building and Stowe Cottage at the southern loop. Farm buildings, a superintendent's house, dwellings, a milk house, coops and a pump house with cistern stand in the south-west, with a six-inch water pipe running in from the reservoir. The notes at the top describe the water supply by gravity from a reservoir half a mile north-west of Paddock Hall and the fire appliances. The rest of the grounds is open land in blocks numbered 51 to 58.
notes: Today the Edna Mahan Correctional Facility for Women; its internal roads are unnamed service roads in OpenStreetMap.

Placed from three hand-picked points along B Court matched to modern service-road junctions (B Court with 1st Place and with 2nd Place) and the centre of the modern turning circle at its north end; all three lie on one line, so the placement is a helmert fit and low confidence.
The fitted rotation (about 11 degrees) suggests the north arrow points to magnetic rather than true north.

New Jersey Reformatory for Women (today Edna Mahan Correctional Facility), 1 3/4 miles west of the post office, 100 ft to an inch, north up. Arbitrary internal roads only (A Court, B Court, 1st Place, 2nd Place); no named modern street junction.

sheet-5-1.description: The village of Annandale, about two miles north-east of Clinton, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the top. The part covers the village grid between Main Street and the Central Railroad of New Jersey in the north and Beaver Avenue and Beaver Brook in the south, from Maple Avenue in the west to East Street in the east. Main runs east from West Street past Center Street to the C.R.R. of N.J. passenger depot and freight depot, where several tracks curve across the north of the sheet. Between Main and Beaver Avenue the blocks along West, Center and East Streets, Roosevelt Place and Washington Place are lined with frame dwellings on long narrow lots. Commerce is small: stores and a hardware and confectionery shop near Main and Center, the Hummeer and Smith printing works on West Street, a furniture and plumbing store on Washington Place, and the B. W. Farrington lumber and coal yard with lumber sheds and coal pockets beside the railroad. North of Main are the F. G. Sharps Annandale Creamery and a fertilizer shed by Silver Lake, and a fire department house stands on West Street. The Reformed Church faces Beaver Avenue at West Street. South of Beaver Avenue, Old Allerton Road (West) and New Allerton Road (South) lead out of the village; a public school stands on New Allerton Road and an older public school, marked not used, near Old Allerton Road. The north-east corner shows the office and laboratory of the Annandale Graphite Corporation and a six-inch water pipe from the reservoir, and the sheet's note gives Annandale's population as 500, its water supply from Clinton and its volunteer hose company. The graphite works itself is drawn in a separate inset in the upper left corner.
notes: Roosevelt Place is now Roosevelt Avenue and Washington Place is Washington Street in OpenStreetMap.
Old Allerton Road (West), the continuation of West south of Beaver Avenue, is now Lower West Street; New Allerton Road (South), opposite Maple Avenue, is now the north end of Humphrey Road.
East Street's modern junctions with Beaver Avenue and Main Street lie 15 m or more from the drawn ones and were not used as control.
The Raritan Valley Line follows the C.R.R. of N.J. tracks drawn across the north of the sheet.

Annandale at 100 ft to an inch, north up: Main, West, Center, East, Maple Avenue, Roosevelt Place, Washington Place, Beaver Avenue, Old and New Allerton Roads, C.R.R. of N.J. depots. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset at upper left, Annandale Graphite Corp. works, located 3/10 mile north-east of the station.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Annandale Graphite Corp. works, 3/10 mile north-east of the station (no street junction or road).
